item.description: A large sign announces the Texas State Championship competition in Girls Flag Football along the sidelines of one of the playing fields. The girls high school flag football championship tournament was held at the University of North Texas DATCU Stadium in Denton on June 13, 2026. (Steve Hamm/The Dallas Morning News) Girls flag football is one step closer to becoming a UIL-sanctioned sport. The UIL legislative council approved a proposal to begin a girls flag football pilot program, beginning in the 2028-29 school year with no more than two conferences. The proposal needs final approval from the Texas Commissioner of Education. As of fall 2027, 25 states will have sanctioned girls flag football. A superintendent survey conducted by the UIL this fall found that 52% of Class 6A and 5A superintendents support the adoption of flag football as a sanctioned sport. The survey also found that 165 schools currently offer the sport. The Houston Texans and the Dallas Cowboys have been advocating for the addition of girls flag football as a sanctioned UIL sport for multiple years. Flag football is quickly growing across the country at all levels. The NCAA added flag football to its Emerging Sports for Women program in January, which gives the sport a pathway to become an NCAA-sanctioned activity. Sports like rowing, beach volleyball and water polo have previously gone through the program and are now NCAA-championship sports. item.title: Fantasy Football Impact: Josh Jacobs' Status For Week 7 Is To Be Determined
item.description: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) stiff-arms Cincinnati Bengals cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt (29) on Sunday, October 12, 2025, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. The Packers won the game, 27-18. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect After a six-week-long wait, fantasy football owners are chomping at the bit to see Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs back on the field and get him back in their lineups. However, there is a chance that they could have to wait beyond Week 7. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that he will get a full week of practice, but he is not a lock to play next week after missing so much time. LaFleur said he's been training, but his status is still to be determined: "We feel like he's in a pretty good spot. He's been training, but he's missed the exposure to football." Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs will practice on Wednesday and get a full week of work but TBD on whether he'll play on Sunday at Detroit. "We feel like he's in a pretty good spot. He's been training, but he's missed the exposure to football." - Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 19, 2026 Fantasy Impact RB Josh Jacobs, Green Bay Packers We expect Jacobs to be out there in Week 7. It would be a shock if they held him out for a week to get in shape. If he's been training, he should be in good enough shape to get on the field. Jacobs has shown us nothing in his career on the field that would lead us to believe that he has been sitting on his coach eating Cheese Doodles and not keeping in shape for a return. However, there is a chance that he could take a week to ramp up in a more split workload. He won't necessarily be on a snap count, but he also probably won't see a full bell-cow workload. While we expect him to be in shape, being in shape and handling a near-every-down role in an NFL game are very different. If you have Jacobs and he's active, you can safely start him this week. The other running backs in Green Bay have been horrible, and they could need Jacobs out there to defeat the Detroit Lions in Week 7. RB MarShawn Lloyd, Green Bay Packers After a mostly disastrous six weeks, you can now drop all those useless Packers' backup running backs. You can safely cut Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. There is no reason to hold them and clog up a roster spot because we've already seen how they look if Jacobs goes down, and it's not good. It's certainly not worth holding them as handcuffs just in case. item.title: Serie A | Parma 0-3 Torino: Simeone double spoils Gilardino’s Tardini bow
item.description: Serie A | Parma 0-3 Torino: Simeone double spoils Gilardino’s Tardini bow Giovanni Simeone struck twice and Che Adams headed in as Torino spoiled Alberto Gilardino’s first home game in charge of Parma with a 3-0 win at the Tardini. Gilardino’s Parma went into the game on four points after a 3-0 defeat at Inter, and were without Hans Nicolussi Caviglia, Pontus Almqvist and Elphege, who had surgery for appendicitis. Adrián Bernabé returned to the midfield, with Giovanni Fabbian also starting. Ignazio Abate’s Torino had beaten Udinese last time out but were missing Niccolò Fortini and Emirhan Ilkhan. Ardian Ismajli came into the defence in place of Ricardo Rodríguez. Torino made a fast start. Adams had a volley blocked inside the opening minute and Saúl Coco headed off target from the resulting corner. They went ahead on four minutes, when Rafik Belghali lofted a cross into the box and Simeone met it with a left-footed finish into the top corner. Pietro Comuzzo headed wide from close range before Torino doubled their lead on 24 minutes. Simeone’s shot was blocked and Adams reacted first to nod home the rebound, with the goal surviving a VAR check for offside. Parma did respond. Lucas Perri made a superb diving save to keep out David Romero, then gathered headers from Diego Carlos and Fabbian. Enrico Delprato should have pulled one back just before the break, but steered wide from inside the six-yard box. PARMA, ITALY – OCTOBER 19: Nikola Vlasic of Torino FC runs with the ball during the Serie A match between Parma Calcio and Torino FC at Stadio Ennio Tardini on October 19, 2026 in Parma, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) Parma pile on the pressure but Torino put the game to bed Gilardino made a double change at half-time, bringing on Dominik Drobnič and Simone Lontani. El Bilal Touré headed narrowly wide, Lontani fired over, and Perri saved from Bernabé and Mariano Troilo. Sascha Britschgi was booked for diving. Romero curled just past the far post before Torino put the game to bed on 69 minutes. Simeone collected Belghali’s headed pass and unleashed a fierce strike from distance into the top corner. Substitute Matija Frigan thought he had pulled one back from Djibril Diallo’s pass, but VAR ruled it out for offside. Perri then comfortably held his effort after a solo run late on. Parma 0-3 Torino Simeone 4, 69 (T), Adams 24 (T)

item.title: Who's Field Hockey Player of the Week, presented by White Plains Hospital?
item.description: Since the beginning of fall season, readers have selected the lohud Field Hockey Player of the Week, sponsored by White Plains Hospital. Last week's winner was Ava Galati, a Clarkstown South senior, who excelled at midfield and on offensive and defensive corners over two games, including during a win over Suffern. She joined earlier winners Alina Cavajani of Panas, Alexa Butler of Clarkstown, Taylor Stillwaggon of Mahopac, Sophia Gac of Valhalla and Lila Walsh of North Rockland. This week, coaches have nominated seven athletes for their Oct. 12-18 play. Their accomplishments are noted below. The poll will close at 3 p.m. Wednesday. Micalyn Kelly, White Plains The senior midfielder, who leads her team in assists with 14 and has been a consistent force on offense, picked up three assists in a 7-1 win over Rye Neck and scored in the Tigers' 4-1 win over Fox Lane. Aimee Kovacs, Somers The Tuskers senior netminder recorded her ninth and 10th shutouts of the season last week. She stopped four shots in a 1-0 win over Scarsdale and earlier in the week, on Somers Senior Night, she shut down Arlington, making nine saves in a 2-0 Tusker win. Kayleigh Pontillo, Mahopac The senior forward scored both the game-tying and overtime game-winning goal in a 3-2 win over Pelham. With the OT winner, Pontillo dribbled past two Pelicans defensemen and scored after going in one-on-one on the Pelham goalie. Millie Nemser, Rye Country Day The junior forward set a Rye Country Day School record by recording two hat tricks in a single week. She had three goals in a 4-1 win over St. Luke's before putting another three in in a 5-2 win over Holy Child. Leah Schaedler, Nanuet The senior midfielder was a force on offense last week, scoring four goals and recording an assist, She scored twice in the Golden Knights/ 7-0 win over Byram Hills, scored in a 4-3 loss to Hastings, registered the assist in a 4-2 win over Croton/Hen Hud and scored in a 3-1 loss to Pawling. Elizabeth Torres, Suffern Coming off a week in which she scored twice, including netting an overtime game-winner, the senior midfielder again scored twice and added two assists in a 7-1 win over Nyack. The following day, she returned to overtime heroics, scoring with five seconds left in OT as the Mounties edged Pleasantville 2-1. Luca Vecchiariello, Pleasantville The senior is an upper defenseman, whose role is critical in stopping opponents' initial advances down the field. She excelled doing that in a 2-1 win over Ursuline. Vecchiariello made multiple block tackles, stole the ball multiple times and, dodging opponents, helped create multiple offensive chances for the Panthers. Nancy Haggerty covers sports for The Journal News/lohud . item.title: Ronaldo given 30-day suspension and £215 fine by Portuguese FA
item.description: Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances [Getty Images] Cristiano Ronaldo has been given a 30-day suspension and fined 255 euros (£215) by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving his country's international camp last month. The 41-year-old captain walked out of Portugal's Nations League squad in September after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark on 1 October. Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement he had left because Portugal coach Jorge Jesus twice "broke his word", accusing him of an "absolute breach of trust". The Al-Nassr forward's suspension takes effect from the day of the Denmark match, meaning he has already served 19 days of his ban and will complete it by the end of the month. The FPF disciplinary committee said it took into account "the remorse shown" by Ronaldo in his statement. He accepted accountability and apologised to his team-mates and fans for his actions, before adding he deserved to be punished. Portugal boss Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but has left the door open for his return. Pedro Proenca, president of the FPF, told Portuguese outlet Record there is a "strong desire" to have Ronaldo back with the national team once the matter is resolved. The five-time Ballon d'Or winner has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances - both men's world records - helping them win Euro 2016 and the two Nations League titles. He joined Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr in December 2022 on a reported annual salary of £177m and signed a contract extension last year. item.title: Building Lionesses 2.0 - Wiegman's new challenge awaits
item.description: Sarina Wiegman has won the past three Women's European Championships - with the Netherlands in 2017 and England in 2022 and 2025 [Getty Images] When Sarina Wiegman took the reins as England manager in September 2021, she declared she had "come to bring the next level". Winner of the 2017 Women's Euros with her own Netherlands and runner-up at the subsequent World Cup in 2019, she certainly had the pedigree, but could she deliver on her promises? Five years on, Wiegman has pocketed two more European Championships and acquired another silver medal on the global stage. Not only that, but the success of her Lionesses exploded the women's game in this country, taking it not just to a new level, but to previously unthinkable heights. And yet on the day Wiegman extends her deal until after the Euros in 2029, her newest challenge could be her hardest yet. England manager Wiegman signs contract extension Why must England evolve? [BBC] Wiegman's successful England teams have been built on a core group of players from an outstanding generation - but a few cracks have appeared this year. Seven of the team that started against world champions Spain in June also played in the Euro 2022 final against Germany - and their 4-0 defeat in Mallorca laid bare the gap England must bridge to the world's best. That result also consigned England to two rounds of play-offs to reach next summer's World Cup. Beating Greece this month navigated the first of those, with games against Ukraine, who they have beaten twice already in 2026, to come before Christmas. Nevertheless, finding successors to those who have spearheaded the success will not be straightforward. Defensive stalwarts Lucy Bronze and Alex Greenwood will be 37 and 36 respectively by Euro 2029, while Leah Williamson and Keira Walsh will be 32. Other key players such as Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway will also have turned 30, far from past their best, but still a consideration. "We have to continue the evolution of the Lionesses," record goalscorer Ellen White told the Women's Football Weekly podcast. "We can't stay stagnant or keep trying to win in the same ways all the time." Former England goalkeeper Rachel Brown-Finnis thinks one of Wiegman's strengths as a manager is her willingness to give young players a chance. "She's not afraid of bringing in players who have never been capped before," Brown-Finnis told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Wiegman is looking right across the spectrum and asking who's on form, who can add to my squad, who can fill a position or a couple of different positions?" Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club, former Lionesses captain Steph Houghton said: "You can see Wiegman is trying to change a few things. The last camp she brought on Lexi Potter for her debut and she is now starting regularly for Chelsea. As a young player you need that to thrive in this environment. "She is seeing the progress of young players coming through to press those who have been in the squad for a long time."

item.title: Maresca surpasses Guardiola as City continue perfect league start
item.description: Maresca surpasses Guardiola as City continue perfect league start Enzo Maresca has made Premier League history at Manchester City , becoming the first manager to win his opening seven league games in charge of a club. City maintained their perfect start with Saturday’s 3-2 victory over Ipswich Town, taking their points tally to 21 in 21 possible. Maresca’s side have also claimed wins over Bournemouth , Crystal Palace, Coventry City, Manchester United, Sunderland and Liverpool during their remarkable run. Maresca has surpassed the previous benchmark of six consecutive wins set by Pep Guardiola at City, Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea and Ole Gunnar Solskjær at Manchester United. City have scored 19 goals and conceded six during their opening seven league games, underlining their strength at both ends of the pitch. When it comes to best start to a season, Chelsea set the benchmark with nine straight wins to open the 2005-06 season, while Liverpool came close in 2019-20, winning their first eight matches. Although defeats to Arsenal in the Community Shield and Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League have interrupted their progress elsewhere, Maresca’s domestic start has put City in a strong position early in the season.

item.title: African wonderkid closing in on joining Andoni Iraola's Liverpool first-team
item.description: African wonderkid closing in on joining Andoni Iraola's Liverpool first-team Andoni Iraola's first-team could soon be bolstered by an exciting African wonderkid. The Spaniard has been a breath of fresh air since his arrival. Under Arne Slot, Liverpool have lost their identity. The Dutchman may be a good coach but he was simply not the right fit for Liverpool. Slot showed what he was capable of during his first year in charge. However, he also showed what he was not capable of in his second season in charge. When he had to work with a strong squad, and players who had already achieved or come close to fulfiling their potential, Slot flourished. However, when he was forced to develop players, work with youngsters and promote from the academy, he faltered. Slot just didn't seem to be that type of manager. He was a farcry from Jurgen Klopp, who relished working with youngsters. Andoni Iraola's exciting young generation at Liverpool From the get-go Iraola has proven he is different. In pre-season, he was not afraid of throwing a 16-year-old in Joshua Abe at the deep-end. He also gave Ifeanyi Ndukwe an increased playing time, and opted to promote Lewis Koumas after he recognised the Welshman was the perfect fit for his philosophy. Under Iraola, the Reds youngsters are now finally getting chances. Trey Nyoni has had the opportunity to establish himself as a key midfielder. Koumas has become a great source of energy off the bench. And Rio Ngumoha is slowly getting better and better on the right-wing. Iraola is proving that he has that Klopp touch about him. He is able to get the maximum out of all of his players and he is willing to reward younger players the chance to prove themselves. Mor Talla Ndiaye is closing in on the first-team At the same time, Iraola is also having to contend with injury problems. Right now, Jeremie Frimpong has a knock, and Dominik Szoboszlai is also out injured. Injuries usually means an opportunity for someone else who is catching the eye at academy level to be promoted. And one of those players who is now really pushing in earning a promotion to the senior squad is Mor Talla Ndiaye. The Senegalese U17 international has been a revelation since he arrived in the January window earlier this year. He is a commanding and extremely composed defender. Ndiaye recently scored a 92nd minute winner for Liverpool's U21 side against West Brom. He is getting better and better, and it's only a matter of time until Iraola calls him up for the first-team. It very much feels like Ndiaye is on the verge of joining the senior squad.

item.title: Florida is No. 1 again. Last season explains why the Gators still have something to prove
item.description: Florida is No. 1 again. Last season explains why the Gators still have something to prove originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Florida opens the 2026-27 men’s college basketball season atop the AP Top 25, with 47 of 59 first-place votes. The ranking puts the Gators back in familiar territory after their 2025 national championship, but it also brings an uncomfortable recent memory: last season began with Florida at No. 3, then saw the Gators fall out of the poll by early January. They recovered to win the SEC regular-season title, only to lose to Iowa as a No. 1 seed in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. That sharp turn makes this preseason ranking more than a compliment. It is a test of whether Florida can carry lofty expectations through the long middle of the season. The Gators are No. 1 in the men's basketball preseason AP Poll 🏀 https://t.co/5ft3dT7FMH — ESPN (@espn) October 19, 2026 The No. 1 ranking comes with a built-in reminder The Gators have a compelling case. Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon and Rueben Chinyelu are back from the title team, while Denzel Aberdeen returns after spending last season at Kentucky. That gives coach Todd Golden a core that has experienced the biggest stage and the frustration of a season that ended short of its goal. Florida’s returning group is a real advantage in a sport where rosters can change dramatically from one year to the next. But last season showed that experience alone does not make a team immune to a rough stretch. The Gators will need to turn their familiarity with each other into steadier play when the schedule gets difficult. Illinois is No. 3 after receiving the other two. Florida has a strong lead in the vote, but the poll offers no guarantees once the games begin. UConn and Arizona round out the top five, giving the preseason ranking a crowded championship conversation from the start. Golden has said the program should expect to compete at this level. That is the mindset of a team that has won a title. The challenge is matching that confidence with the consistency Florida lacked last winter. The No. 1 spot is a headline today; keeping the Gators there will take months of work. item.title: Nic Claxton Out Two Weeks Leaves Bulls With Thin Frontcourt
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images The Chicago Bulls are starting their season without their big man. Nic Claxton will miss at least the first two weeks of the regular season due to a hamstring injury suffered in the preseason. This is a major hit for a team that needs size. Coach Tiago Splitter confirmed the timeline on Monday after the medical staff re-evaluated the center this week. Splitter knows fans want a hard date. He told the media that he cannot give one. “This is not a science,” Splitter said. “I wish I could tell you guys, ‘Hey, 13 (days) left and then he’s going to play.’ It’s not like that. Everybody’s different. Everybody reacts to treatment different. Everybody reacts to practice different.”. The coach tried to be clear about the average recovery time. “On average, he should be back in two weeks. But that’s all I can do.”. Smith Steps Into the Starting Role Jalen Smith is the guy who has to fill the gap right now. He will start in the lineup while Claxton sits on the bench. Smith started most of the Bulls’ preseason games and should keep that role for the opener. This sets up a solid workload for him to open the season. The team opens Wednesday against the Raptors in Toronto. Smith has to be ready to lead the defense immediately. There is no time to warm up. The injury situation is not just about Claxton. Zach Collins is also sidelined by a quadriceps injury. Collins might return for Wednesday’s opener after practicing without limitations in Monday’s short session. According to the Chicago Tribune , Collins has not received clearance to play Wednesday. Collins was not restricted in Monday’s practice, which sets him up to be available for the game. The Bulls are hoping for a quick return, but the frontcourt is thin. Rebuild Patience Tested Early The Chicago Tribune reports the Bulls expect Claxton to be ready by the first week of November. item.title: Marion Harding boys win a championship, plus more league XC results
item.description: Marion Harding was pointing to Oct. 17 all season. The Presidents felt they could win a Mid Ohio Athletic Conference boys cross country championship on their own course. "Honestly we’ve raced really good this season," Marion Harding coach Bob Peters said. "We made it a point to win the conference this year. I felt like we were racing well against the conference throughout the year when we saw somebody. The guys wanted this. They came in locked-in on this meet." As they envisioned, the Presidents won the title with 46 points to edge Ontairio's 55 and Shelby's 78. Pleasant was fourth with 103 followed by Highland at 105, River Valley at 110 and Galion at 215. It is Harding's first league crown in boys XC in 21 years and its first in the MOAC. "There was a lot of stress coming into this meet because they wanted it so bad," Peters said. "Starting off the day, we were talking that this is just another race. It’s the next race so let’s go out here and do our best and whatever happens, happens. They really worked this whole season for this moment." "We were at the awards area where they were announcing the teams, and they got to second place. I was watching them and you could see the reaction when they announce Ontario second so they knew they won it. It was really good to see them get rewarded for their work they’ve done for this year," the coach said. For Harding's girls, Noel Stidham was the runner-up in 19:45 behind Shelby's Anna Will in 19:19 and just ahead of Pleasant's Madisyn Ruhe in third at 19:47 and Highland's Veronica Ballard in fourth at 19:53. "This is my 10 th year of coaching and that was one of the best races I’ve seen in all the years," Coach Peters said. "It was a great race to watch what she did there and come back like that and run as good as she did. It’s exciting to know she’s got two more years." More from the MOAC boys race Pleasant's Joey Dietsch was the boys individual champion with a 16:20, and River Valley's Kael Swartz was the runner-up in 16:35. Also for Pleasant were Turner Wilson (12th, 17:49), Jacob Meyers (19th, 18:14), Nathan Wagenblast (38th, 19:37) and Adam Stevens (42nd, 19:44). Behind Swartz for RV were Hager Adams (17th, 18:06), William Koon (23rd, 18:37), Harrison Lee (36th, 19:33), Iain Linville (41st, 19:42), Markus Parsons (44th, 19:55) and Brocktyn Caudill (51st, 20:13). He returned against the Jets on Sunday and earned 27 receiving yards. He dropped three attempts for the first time in his career. There appeared to be some rust after missing all that time. Many have wondered if the Patriots already regret trading for Brown. ESPN’s Dan Graziano reacted to that idea, calling it an overreaction. He stated that the team is 4-2 despite Brown's tough start, and "that tells you there's room for things to get a lot better." Coach Mike Vrabel said the team was " lucky to win ” following drops and multiple injuries. Brown later stated there are no excuses and that he’s going to put his best foot forward. The Patriots have a quick turnaround as they head to Chicago to face the Bears on Thursday. Graziano believes there’s nothing in Brown’s history indicating his struggles will continue. item.title: Chiefs Defensive Line Ends Historic Sack Drought
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs were about to join a very small, very unlucky club in NFL history. Entering Sunday’s game, the team was one of only three squads in the Super Bowl era to win three straight games without recording a single sack, according to reports. That ugly streak finally died in the second half. On Sunday, October 18, the defense finally located the quarterback amid the 22-6 victory against the Los Angeles Chargers. The drought ended with less than four minutes left in the third quarter when defensive end Ashton Gillotte tackled Justin Herbert. The Chiefs finished the day with four sacks total. Chris Jones and Peter Woods each got one. Chamarri Conner and George Karlaftis also added sacks late in the fourth quarter. It wasn’t just about the stats, though. The guys in the trenches were clearly frustrated by the lack of production. The Drive to Hit the Quarterback Ashton Gillotte, a second-year defensive end, didn’t hide his hunger for a big play. He told KSHB 41’s Tod Palmer, according to Yahoo Sports , “Obviously, that’s something we’ve been hunting up, and we’ve been longing for it.” He also noted that while “pressures are good, but that’s not what we pride ourselves on.” The pass rush has been inconsistent lately. Linebacker Drue Tranquill told the station that “teams have been getting the ball out quick on us.” It’s hard to live with that kind of efficiency. Still, the pressure is there. Karlaftis produced eight pressures across 38 pass rushes in the contest, according to reports. That was his second-highest single-game total in his career. The defensive front is finding its rhythm again. This season, Gillotte holds nine pressures alongside a 63.4 pass-rush grade as indicated by PFF data. For Woods, the win also marked his first career sack. Injury Concerns for the Offensive Line The win was a bit bittersweet because the cost was high. The Chiefs are already dealing with injuries to wide receivers Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton. Now, the right tackle position is in trouble. Jaylon Moore left the game after a heavy hit during the second quarter. Andy Reid confirmed the news after the game. “Jaylon Moore has a concussion,” Reid said. “That’s the one that stands out the most.” This is a massive blow to the unit. Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports reported that the strain between the two boiled over into an argument before the Bills-Rams game at SoFi Stadium, and Aikman didn’t dispute it when he appeared on KTCK The Ticket in Dallas days later. That same night, Aikman told Jimmy Traina he expected ESPN to go in a different direction , noting that nobody had approached him about a new contract with the Super Bowl in February and his deal expiring in March. Simmons was hazier on the “Miami thing” than on the money, at one point wondering aloud whether Aikman had acquired some kind of ownership stake in the Dolphins. ESPN insisted the arrangement didn’t interfere with his broadcasting duties , and the role was billed as temporary, but Aikman stayed on to help with the head coaching search after McDaniel was fired New head coach Jeff Hafley later described Aikman as a trusted sounding board , and Aikman raised eyebrows across the league by explaining on the Cowboys’ DLLS podcast that Miami valued his relationships and the information he could obtain that the team couldn’t. That arrangement has since wound down, with Mark Maske of Front Office Sports reporting last week that Aikman no longer has a formal, ongoing consulting agreement with Miami, but not before it invited a year’s worth of conflict-of-interest questions about the man calling the league’s Monday night showcase. Aikman’s now-former side gig is a large part of why Simmons can’t summon much sympathy. He pointed out that Aikman calls 17 regular-season games a year, flies around the country to do it, and would see ESPN draw virtually the same audience for those games whether he’s in the booth or not. When Cousin Sal noted that Simmons usually champions talent banding together in negotiations, Simmons granted that Buck and Aikman hadn’t done that, but questioned the assumption that Buck was the one who broke ranks. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty ATLANTA, GEORGIA - APRIL 20: Manager Rocco Baldelli #5 of the Minnesota Twins looks on during the fifth inning against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park on April 20, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 27: Manager Dan Wilson #6 of the Seattle Mariners looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Angels at T-Mobile Park on September 27, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Mariners have another experienced name to consider as they search for a replacement for Dan Wilson. Rocco Baldelli has emerged as a candidate, according to Adam Jude of The Seattle Times, who reported that Seattle is expected to speak with the former Minnesota Twins manager. The connection makes sense. Baldelli managed Minnesota for seven seasons and spent 2026 as a special assistant in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ front office. However, his résumé should only be the start of Seattle’s evaluation. The Mariners need to determine how Baldelli would address this roster’s problems, particularly when deciding who plays, how hitters prepare, and when established plans need to change. That requires specific answers about Seattle’s players before the organization makes another consequential hire. Rocco Baldelli Gives Mariners an Experienced Option Getty Manager Rocco Baldelli #5 of the Minnesota Twins looks on during the fifth inning against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park on April 20, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Baldelli finished his Twins tenure with a 527-505 record and three American League Central titles. He earned AL Manager of the Year honors after Minnesota won 101 games in 2019. His first Twins team also set an MLB record with 307 home runs . Those accomplishments show he can run a successful Major League clubhouse. They do not establish that the same approach would automatically work in Seattle. The Mariners should ask how he would construct consistent roles around Julio Rodríguez, Cal Raleigh and Josh Naylor while bringing younger hitters into the lineup. They should also ask when he would prioritize a platoon advantage and when a player needs an extended opportunity against different pitching. No universal answer exists to either question. A useful interview would require Baldelli to explain his choices using Seattle’s actual roster. That would reveal more than a discussion focused entirely on his previous division championships or the organization he most recently worked for. Seattle should also ask him to describe a decision that failed in Minnesota, the information he used at the time, and what he would change now. That would make the evaluation more concrete. A nickname can spread quickly online, especially when it offers a simple way to describe a public figure, but Cunningham’s own explanation is more complicated than the label suggests. Her situation shows how an athlete’s public identity can take on a life of its own. Once political audiences begin to identify someone with a particular movement or worldview, changing that perception can be difficult, even when the person offers a more nuanced account. Fun fact: Cunningham played college basketball at the University of Missouri, where she became one of the program’s most decorated players and earned multiple All-SEC honors before entering the WNBA. Late in the contest, Cunningham committed a hard foul on Jacy Sheldon, triggering another confrontation in a game that had already featured several physical incidents involving Clark and other players. item.title: Man United’s Diogo Dalot leaves every Premier League defender trailing in remarkable statistic
item.description: Man United’s Diogo Dalot leaves every Premier League defender trailing in remarkable statistic Manchester United star Diogo Dalot has emerged as the standout defender in the Premier League in one remarkable statistic. Dalot’s progress Amid United’s miserable start to the season, Dalot, like so many of his teammates, finds himself stuck in a desperately poor patch of form. Dalot has been in and out of the starting XI in the 10 games United have played so far across all competitions. He has primarily been used in his preferred right-back position, but Michael Carrick deployed him on the left during Sunday’s 1-1 draw with Leeds United at Elland Road. Carrick made tactical changes, deploying Dalot higher up as a left wing-back in an attempt to drag Manchester United out of their pitiful slump in performances and results. Although Dalot was solid defensively, his overall performance remained imperfect, with some elements leaving much to be desired. It was in attack where he fell short most of all, with United missing the thrust from his flank that Amad supplied on the other side. A new statistic has nevertheless suggested that Dalot may actually be one of the most creative defenders in the league. Dalot tops stat According to WhoScored, Dalot has created more chances (14) than any other defender in the Premier League this season. Although the statistic will provide encouragement to Dalot and the fans, it is clear that further effort is required if he is to earn complete trust and establish himself as an assured fixture. Dalot and his teammates are next in action on Wednesday when they face Como in the Champions League. Nothing short of a victory will relieve pressure on Carrick and his players. Carrick still retains the backing of the United board, but a loss would certainly put that faith to the test. Featured image by Stu Forster via Getty Images

That’s usually a scene that isn’t seen by the visiting team. James, though, is the rare player who might want to see it. And hey, he’s LeBron — he could probably do whatever he chooses in this situation. LeBron James Could Make Unusual Decision It would still be very odd to see James out on the floor watching the Knicks celebrate their championship. NBA insider Brian Windhorst, though, thinks it would at least make some sense when considering the entirety of who LeBron is. This is what Windhorst said on the Hoop Collective on Monday: “ LeBron has had four of his own ring nights of his own. And I know the Sixers won’t be out there on the court while the Knicks are accepting their rings and the banner goes up. But I wonder if LeBron would like to be out there just to feel the Garden. He’s praised the Garden 100 times and if you give him 100 more times he would praise it 100 more times. He truly loves the Garden. I wonder if part of him wants to just stand out there just as a fan of the game and as a fan of basketball.” James, as much as any player of this era, is regarded as someone who truly appreciates the history of the game. MSG is a historic venue, called “The Mecca” by those in the city. While it’d be surprising to see James out there on the floor, it’s fascinating to get some insight into his potential thinking from Windhorst, who has covered the King since high school. 76ers-Knicks Schedule These teams are scheduled for a 7 p.m. ET start on Tuesday. With the ring ceremony, the game itself likely won’t tip off at that time. But basketball fans in Philadelphia and New York City won’t mind a few extra minutes of waiting. They’re both amped up for a special season of hoops ahead — the Knicks as defending champs, and the Sixers with their new all-time great. The Green Bay Packers got some huge news prior to their Week 6 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys , as it was revealed that Josh Jacobs would be activated off the NFL's Commissioner Exempt list on Monday after Week 6. Now that the day has come, there are plenty of questions about what Jacob's involvement in the Packers will look like going forward. He's not played in well over a month, so the questions about his workload are very real. Rob Domovsky of ESPN shared a big update on the Packers' plans with Jacobs, as Matt LaFleur revealed Green Bay won't have such a simple plan with Jacobs for Week 7. Packers reveal plan with Josh Jacobs amid return to NFL "Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs will practice on Wednesday and get a full week of work but TBD on whether he'll play on Sunday at Detroit," Demovsky reports. The Packers are going to bring Jacobs up to speed with a full week of work at practice, which is an encouraging sign for Jacobs to return in Week 7. However, LaFleur revealed the team still might not play Jacobs in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions , even if he gets in a full week of work. LaFleur explained, "We feel like he's in a pretty good spot. He's been training, but he's missed the exposure to football." MORE : Aaron Rodgers blasts Buccaneers' field as 'one of the worst surfaces in the league' It seems likely that Green Bay will make him active if they believe he's ready for NFL contact, but if he's not ready to go, they're not afraid of making him a healthy scratch for a week. There is a big difference between working out and staying in shape for an NFL season versus being ready to take on big hits, like Jacobs will as a running back. Jacobs isn't a lock to play in Week 7, but the Packers are intent on working him into the offense during practice to see where he's at. If all goes well, then Jacobs might play. This plan from the Packers makes perfect sense. It's a long season, and sitting at 4-2, the Packers should have no reason to rush Jacobs back if he's not 100% ready to go. item.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ,” the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . It had been a frustrating week, domestically and continentally, in two games on the road. On both occasions they had been caught cold, conceding the Bundesliga’s fastest goal at Augsburg and going 1-0 down in less than 90 seconds in Stavanger . Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, almost motionless in his seat as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. The sporting director, Max Eberl, who stood in for his coach in the post-match press conference, explained that the Belgian had been ill, not to mention Kompany’s current hip problem that had made the move from dressing room to pitchside slow and uncomfortable. item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
